title: ipfs mcp GET /auth/session response
description: Body of the 200 answer of GET /auth/session (console-session-auth 1.3, ADR-0013 section 4). It reports what the verified session token resolves to and nothing else: the principals it can resolve to (name and kind), the email claim for display, the token's exp, and the admin step-up state. It never carries the token, the `sub` claim or any other claim; additionalProperties false is what makes a body that holds a `sub` or a `token` fail validation. `email` is display-only and never selects or grants a principal.

kind.description: The principal kind. Only the kinds that accept a subject mapping appear (principals[].subjects).

principals.description: Every principal the token's subject maps to, one entry per principal. A valid token whose subject maps to no principal is answered 403 and has no body of this shape.

email.description: The `email` claim, for display only ("Signed in as"). Absent when the token has none. Never used to select a principal.

exp.description: The token's `exp` claim, in seconds since the Unix epoch. The verdict, and so the session, ends no later than this.

admin.description: ok: the subject maps to an admin principal and the token satisfies its require_amr and max_auth_age. step_up_required: it maps to one but fails either check, so a settings request would answer 403 step_up_required. not_eligible: the subject maps to no admin principal.
